text: Hypnogenic, -genetic, -genous [Gr. upnoV , sleep, + genesiV , production]: Ger. schlafbringend , hypnogen ; Fr. hypnogène ; Ital. ipnogeno . Sleep-producing; more specifically applied to agencies which induce the hypnotic state. The term is applied to the physical accessories that are used in the production of the hypnotic state, such as the strained fixation of a bright object, rotating mirrors, a sudden light or sound, stroking the face or hands, &c.; also the mental methods of suggestion, direct or indirect. (See HYPNOSIS). ( J.J. )
